where: Section 2, and the answer to Quiz Q4
problem: The claim 'Any view with an android:id writes its own state into that Bundle' and the follow-up 'my text vanishes on rotation only hits views you built in code without an id' is wrong for TextView. A TextView saves its text only when freezesText is on (EditText, being editable, is on by default). So a TextView declared in XML with an id and filled from code loses its text on rotation too. Quiz Q4 gives the right outcome but the wrong reason: the text is lost because a plain TextView does not freeze its text, not because the view has no id.
fix: Say: views with an android:id save their own state, but what each view chooses to save differs. EditText saves typed text, CheckBox saves its tick, ScrollView saves its scroll position; a plain TextView saves its text only if android:freezesText="true" is set. In Quiz Q4, answer: the EditText survives because it saves its text; the TextView loses its text even if given an id, unless freezesText is set or you store the string yourself in onSaveInstanceState.

problem: The listed order onPause, onStop, onDestroy, then onCreate, onStart, onResume is correct, but the question asks for the callbacks an activity receives in order on rotation, and onSaveInstanceState belongs in that sequence between onPause and onStop. A student copying the answer into an exam may lose a mark for omitting it.
fix: answer: onPause, onSaveInstanceState (called only if the activity is being recreated or stopped, not on Back/finish), onStop, onDestroy on the old instance, then onCreate (with the Bundle), onStart, onRestoreInstanceState, onResume on the new one.
